name: shelf
description: One lens over everything the fleet keeps. Seventy-two modules write their state into ~/.mod/<name> by convention and without supervision, and it is 31 gigabytes; the shared store under ~/.mod/store is the fleet's actual database, holding wasmland's artifacts, listings, runs and ledger and the blobs/ prefix the arena reads from. Nothing could see any of it. shelf accounts for the space (which module, what inside it, which single files), browses and greps the shared store, and rehashes every content-addressed file to check that the bytes still prove the name they are filed under — the one check a content-addressed store cannot skip, and which nothing was doing. It also finds blobs no record refers to, the same bytes filed in two places, and freezes a root under a deterministic CID that can be inspected and restored. It reads: gc, restore and rm are dry runs until confirmed, and it holds no index, cache or database of its own, so it cannot go stale or disagree with the disk. Redaction lives on the read path — secret files are never opened, secret fields come back as fingerprints that reveal whether two modules share a key without revealing the key — and both halves bind loopback with route false, because a state browser on a public port is a credential exfiltrator with a console.
route_note: deliberately unrouted: this reads every module's private state, including key material. Reach it over an SSH tunnel, not the gateway.
backend: src/api/api.py (stdlib http.server — no framework, so the diagnostic still starts when the box is unwell)
frontend: src/app/server.py (stdlib — serves the console at /shelf on :50571 and proxies /shelf/_api to the API)
reads: ~/.mod — every module's state directory, and the shared store at ~/.mod/store
state: none. Every answer is computed from the directory when it is asked; there is no index, cache or database, so this module cannot disagree with the disk.

writes.gc: deletes orphaned blobs — dry until confirm=True, and age-gated even then
writes.rm: deletes one key — dry until confirm=True, and never a secret file
writes.restore: unpacks a snapshot — dry until confirm=True, never overwrites unless told

redaction.where: src/redact.py, on the API read path — not in the page, which would be one curl from irrelevant
redaction.files: server.secret, owner.json, *.pem, .env and anything under vault/ keys/ wallets/ .ssh/ are never opened
redaction.fields: names containing secret, token, key, password, seed, mnemonic, auth… return sha256:xxxxxxxx (Nb)
redaction.why_a_fingerprint: it answers 'do two modules share this key' and 'did it rotate' without the bytes leaving the box

depends.localfs: optional — snapshots pin to it. Every other verb works without it.
depends.store: core/store writes the directory this reads; shelf is a lens, not a second store

not_the_store_mod: core/store is the store. This is named shelf because module names are path-derived and core overwrites orbit in the tree, so anything at orbit/store resolves to core/store and is unreachable dead code.
